body: Looking through the history this code has been here quite some time. The condition around the afterFind call was added in eb02ec4ca938996ac3fd6e3281c8cadf7290e54e, while the afterFind call itself was added in 056c4cc0546e18ddb1848368cc1a154aabfff80b.

From the links, I can see that `afterFind()` appeared twice in the code:
1. with explicit `$primary = false`
   https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/eb02ec4ca938996ac3fd6e3281c8cadf7290e54e/cake/libs/model/datasources/dbo_source.php#L689
2. with implicit `$primary = false`
   https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/eb02ec4ca938996ac3fd6e3281c8cadf7290e54e/cake/libs/model/datasources/dbo_source.php#L853

And I believe `afterFind()` for the primary model was called from the very model class back then.

It was added in the second one, inside `queryAssociation()`, to honor the callback for deep models, when in recursive mode.

Back then `__filterResults()` (wich called `afterFind()`) was called [only from `read()`](https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/056c4cc0546e18ddb1848368cc1a154aabfff80b/cake/libs/model/datasources/dbo_source.php#L600-L628), and all the magic was there.

Now, we still have those two `_filterResults()`, and two more inside `queryAssociation()` (with all its recursiveness), and we still have the same two `afterFind()` calls we had before.

I'm trying hard to understand every bit of code in actual `read()`, `_filterResults()` and `queryAssociation()` but at some point I fail miserably, I think there are many undocumented bits (and probably edge cases) there.

Can you hint me what should be the purpose of those functions? I feel they don't have a clear separation of concern right now so they end up repeating some logic and doing unneeded stuff too.

I doubt anyone really understands how that code wrks anymore. The code was originally untested and undocumented and has been patched and modified many times over the years. I don't actually fully understand the code myself to be honest.
Hahaha, good to know! Is it being rewritten for 3.0? Is it worth trying to disjoin some of the spaguetti?¿
@bar yes, it was already rewritten for 3.0

I'm troubled by this exact issue. I think it should be a "bug" somehow: by no means the same `afterFind()` callback should be called on the same set of data, which will bring problems like double-escaping.

I know you guys are rewriting this part of code in 3.0, but forgive me to ask that will you try to fix this problem in the 2.x series? 3.0 is not coming right away and I'm afraid I don't want to upgrade my whole big project immediately. It is great if this issue can be fixed in 2.x series.

In my opinion, the bug lies in the second call, the `queryAssociation()`, and maybe it has something to do with Containable Behaviour details below:

I have an Event model which 'belongsTo' Category model. If I directly do a `find()` in the Event model, everything is OK. I can only see one `afterFind()` callback from `_filterResults()`. However, in another `HotEvent` model(which is also Containable), if I do a find() with contain like:

``` php
$this->find('first', array(
  'contain' => array(
    'Event' => array(
    'fields' => array(...),
    'Category' => array('fields' => array(...))
  )
));
```

I will see two `afterFind()` callback in Event model. First is from `_filterResults()`, same as the normal condition. The `$results` array only contains fields in Event model, which looks like:

``` php
array(
  'Event' => array(
    'id' => ...,
    ...
  )
)
```

But there is a second call from `queryAssociation()` with a different `$results` containing both original Event fields(already processed by the first callback) and fields from Category as well, and missing the top layer 'Event' key. Looks like:

``` php
array(
  'id' => ...,
  'name' => ...,
  'Category' => array(
    'id' => ...
  )
)
```

I don't think it is necessary(or 'correct') to call the `Event->afterFind()` on such kind of data. The 'Category' part should and has been processed by `Category->afterFind()`.

isn't it called twice because one is with primary and the other without?

@lorenzo Not really I think. I dumped out the `$primary` parameter, and both are `false`, which I think is correct because the _primary_ find here is the one in another model (say `HotEvent`), and calls in `Event` model and `Category` model are all secondary.
Can you try modifying this block of code https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/2.5/lib/Cake/Model/Datasource/DboSource.php#L1322-L1324 so that it skips belongsTo associations as well?

I've updated my comment to make it clearer. The problem rises when I do find in the `HotEvent` model.

And I also noticed that in the second call, the `$results` has one less hierarchy, missing the top most `Event`.

@Hexcles Please read the first comments in this very issue. They are dirty hacks, and it is in `2.5`, not `2.4`.

As @markstory stated earlier, the code was written 6 years ago, that time it must have been correct, it may not be now, and it was never updated later.
